statement: Pskov, as a junior partner and later dependency of Novgorod, shared in Novgorod's indirect relationship with the Golden Horde — paying tribute through Novgorod's collection mechanism rather than directly. Pskov's position on the western frontier (adjacent to the Teutonic/Livonian Order and Lithuania) meant its military concerns were primarily western, while the Mongol fiscal relationship was mediated through Novgorod. When Moscow absorbed Novgorod (1478), Pskov's Mongol-tributary relationship ended; Pskov was then absorbed by Vasili III (1510) through the same administrative consolidation that had ended Novgorodian independence.
